cover.title: Paste a list and fix a red error
cover.overview: Paste a short list into your page, then cause one red error on purpose, read it, and fix it.
cover.audience: New writers. Do the work in Oxygen, or on the labeled mock if the app cannot open.

blocks.body: Paste a short list into your page, then cause one red error on purpose, read it, and fix it.

blocks.heading: What today is
blocks.body: About 90 minutes. Do the lab in the app. The check at the end uses words from today only.

blocks.heading: Paste, then look
blocks.body: Paste is useful and messy. After a paste, glance at **Text** view. If the list looks like a list, you are fine. If it looks like leftover website code, undo and make the list with the toolbar.

blocks.heading: Break it on purpose
blocks.body:
In Text, delete one closing tag. Read the red line. Write it down. **Undo**.

That red line is not a personal insult. It is the app saying the skeleton does not match.

blocks.heading: Outline
blocks.body: The **Outline** panel (often on the right) lists the pieces of the page. Click a paragraph there to jump. If you cannot find it, skip it. It is a helper, not the lesson.

blocks.title: WYSIWYG XML Editing
watchFor: The error list under the page

lessons.title: Paste, then repair one red line

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
This lab can fail. Fail when: You left the file broken, or you clicked a magic fix you cannot explain, or you never read the error message.

Expected: The list is in the page. You quoted one red error. You undid it. The file opens clean.

blocks.intro: Walk the steps in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: Open your hello-concept.dita from week1/ (or the sample if yours is missing).

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Copy a short three-item list from any browser page.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Paste it into the body in Author. Oxygen should turn it into a list. If it pastes as a blob of text, make a simple list with the toolbar instead.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Switch to Text. Look at the tags around the list. Do not panic.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: In Text, delete one closing tag on purpose. Read the red error. Write the exact message in oxygen-bootcamp-work/day-05-error.txt. Then Undo.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.body: Save. The page should open with no red error.

blocks.summary: The list is in the page. You quoted one red error. You undid it. The file opens clean.

blocks.q: A yellow bulb offers to “fix” the error. When do you click it?
options: Only when you can say what it will change
blocks.why: Some fixes are fine. Some rewrite the page. If you cannot say what will change, Undo is cheaper.

blocks.q: You deleted a closing tag in Text. The file is “not well-formed.” That means…
options: The tags no longer match, so the file is broken as XML
The shop will not like your wording
blocks.why: Well-formed means the tags nest and match. It is about the skeleton, not about spelling.
